name: Ralph J Andretta
current_role: President and CEO and director, Bread Financial Holdings (NYSE: BFH), Columbus, Ohio
profile: Card-industry executive who became CEO of Alliance Data Systems in February 2020 and led its transformation into Bread Financial, a tech-forward consumer credit/payments company. Earlier he was Managing Director and Head of U.S. Cards at Citi, held affinity and international card roles at Bank of America, and spent 18 years at American Express. Wealth is from BFH equity.
interesting_fact: He steered Alliance Data's reinvention: spinning off its loyalty business and renaming the company Bread Financial in 2022, refocusing it on private-label/co-brand credit cards and the Bread Pay buy-now-pay-later platform.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career with an 18-year run at American Express before moving to Bank of America and Citi, and holds a bachelor's degree in accounting and finance from Siena College.
notes: Public-company CEO; route via Bread Financial media relations (Rachel Stultz). Fintech/consumer credit angle rather than energy.

name: Michael George Rosenbaum
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and director, Guidewire Software (NYSE: GWRE); director, DocuSign
profile: Mike Rosenbaum has been CEO of Guidewire, the property-and-casualty insurance core-systems software company, since August 2019, leading its shift to the Guidewire Cloud platform and AI tools for insurers. Before that he spent about 14 years at Salesforce, latterly as EVP of Product for its core CRM clouds. He also sits on DocuSign's board.
interesting_fact: Before tech, he was a US Navy submarine officer; he holds a B.S. in Systems Engineering from the US Naval Academy and an MBA from UC Berkeley's Haas School.
deep_cut_fact: At Salesforce he ran product management and go-to-market strategy for the core CRM products (EVP Product, 2016-2019) before being recruited to run Guidewire.
notes: Do not confuse with Michael Rosenbaum, founder of Catalyte/Arena Analytics (different person). Contacts read from Guidewire press-release media block via search tool (site blocked direct fetch); re-check before use. Media: Melissa Cobb, Director of PR.

name: William Iwaschuk
current_role: Co-President, Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary, Cipher Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: CIFR; formerly Cipher Mining), New York
profile: Will Iwaschuk is a securities/trading lawyer who joined Cipher Mining as Chief Legal Officer in August 2021 and became Co-President in March 2023. Cipher, which began as a Texas bitcoin miner, has rebranded as Cipher Digital and now develops industrial-scale data-center campuses leased to hyperscale/AI tenants. His wealth comes from CIFR equity.
interesting_fact: He is part of the leadership pivoting Cipher from bitcoin mining to hyperscale data centers, including a long-term lease at its Barber Lake, Texas campus that the company says will bring over $9 billion of revenue.
deep_cut_fact: A Canadian-trained lawyer (LL.B. and B.A., University of British Columbia), he began as an equity derivatives associate at Davis Polk, spent 2005-2012 in Goldman Sachs' legal department, was General Counsel of HFT firm Tower Research Capital, and sits on the board of the Texas Blockchain Council.

name: Robert J Weyers
current_role: Independent director, Nicolet Bankshares (NYSE: NIC), Green Bay, Wisconsin; co-owner of Weyers Group, Commercial Horizons, Inc. and PBJ Holdings, LLC
profile: Robert Weyers (61) is a Wisconsin real-estate developer and private-equity investor and a founding board member of Nicolet National Bank, on whose board he has served since 2000. He co-owns Weyers Group (private equity), Commercial Horizons (commercial property development) and PBJ Holdings (real estate). His insider wealth reflects Nicolet stock, which grew through acquisitions such as MidWestOne in 2026.
interesting_fact: He is one of Nicolet's founding directors (board member since 2000), helping build a de novo Green Bay bank into a multi-state regional bank that closed its acquisition of MidWestOne Financial Group in February 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Nicolet's 2026 proxy cites his commercial real-estate development experience through Commercial Horizons, Inc. as a key board qualification; he also serves on Nicolet's Trust and Wealth Management committees.

name: Ingrid A Estrada
current_role: Senior Vice President and Chief Supply Chain and Operations Officer, Keysight Technologies (NYSE: KEYS), Santa Rosa, California
profile: Ingrid Estrada (61) is a long-time HP/Agilent/Keysight executive and a named executive officer of Keysight, the electronic test & measurement company. She led HR at Keysight from its 2013-14 spin-off from Agilent, served as Chief People and Administrative Officer and Chief of Staff (2017-2025), and since May 2025 runs supply chain and operations. Wealth is from Keysight equity.
interesting_fact: She has run three very different functions at Keysight: global sourcing (at Agilent), the company's HR/people function from the spin-off onward, and now its worldwide supply chain and operations.
deep_cut_fact: Before moving into HR, she was Vice President and General Manager of Global Sourcing at Agilent (2011-2013), so her 2025 move to Chief Supply Chain and Operations Officer was a return to her procurement roots.
notes: Corporate operator, low public profile. Route via Keysight editorial contact (Mark Price). Web search budget exhausted; facts from SEC filings.

name: Richard A Galanti
current_role: Retired EVP and CFO of Costco Wholesale; independent director of Affirm Holdings (AFRM) and Medline, Inc. (MDLN)
profile: Richard Galanti (70) was Costco's chief financial officer for nearly four decades, from January 1985 (after joining as VP Finance in March 1984) until March 2024, and a Costco director 1995-2025; he retired as EVP in January 2025. Earlier he was an investment banker at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette. He now serves on the boards of Affirm (since 2025) and Medline.
interesting_fact: He was one of the longest-serving CFOs of any major US company, running Costco's finances for ~39 years and becoming the familiar voice of Costco's earnings calls from its early days through its growth into a global retail giant.
deep_cut_fact: He left investment banking at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette to join Costco in March 1984 as Vice President, Finance, months after its first warehouse opened, and was CFO by January 1985; he stayed through the 1993 merger with The Price Company.
notes: Retired from Costco; no personal channels found. Reachable only indirectly via Affirm/Medline board (corporate press). Strong retail/finance storyteller. Web search budget exhausted, so no personal-interview anecdotes verified.

Reynolds (61) is one of Amazon's listed executive officers and has been its Worldwide Controller and Principal Accounting Officer since April 2007, signing off on Amazon's financial statements through its growth from an online retailer into AWS, advertising and logistics. name: Scott Gordon
current_role: Executive Chairman and Co-Chief Investment Officer, Chicago Atlantic BDC (Nasdaq: LIEN); Partner, Chicago Atlantic; director, WM Technology (Weedmaps)
profile: Scott Gordon is a veteran emerging-markets investor turned cannabis-finance entrepreneur. After JP Morgan, Marathon, Caxton, Taconic and Fintech Advisory, he co-founded Papa & Barkley parent Egg Rock Holdings, then founded Silver Spike Capital and the SPAC that took Weedmaps public. Silver Spike's BDC became Chicago Atlantic BDC in 2024; it agreed in June 2026 to merge with Chicago Atlantic Real Estate Finance.
interesting_fact: As CEO of Silver Spike Acquisition Corp., he led the SPAC that merged with Weedmaps in 2021, creating WM Technology, one of the first US-listed cannabis tech companies, and he still sits on its board.
deep_cut_fact: Straight out of Bowdoin College in 1983 he was a founding member of JP Morgan's Emerging Markets business; decades later he co-founded Egg Rock Holdings, parent of the Papa & Barkley cannabis brand.

name: Steven McKnight
current_role: Professor (and former chair, 1996-2016) of Biochemistry, UT Southwestern Medical Center, Dallas
profile: Steven L. McKnight (b. 1949) is a molecular biologist known for discovering the leucine-zipper family of transcription factors (C/EBP) and identifying HIF2-alpha. He founded Peloton Therapeutics to drug HIF2-alpha; Merck acquired it in 2019, and its drug belzutifan (Welireg) was approved for kidney cancer. He now studies low-complexity protein domains and phase separation.
interesting_fact: He received the 2025 Albert Lasker Basic Medical Research Award; his HIF2-alpha discovery went from his UT Southwestern lab via Peloton Therapeutics to an FDA-approved cancer drug (belzutifan).
deep_cut_fact: Raised in El Paso, he dropped out of UT Austin after a year, enlisted in the Army and served on a tank crew in Vietnam (adopting a dog that became the crew's mascot) before returning to finish his degree; he credits the Army with giving him 'a sense of purpose and discipline.'
notes: Hurun 'Peloton' = Peloton Therapeutics (biotech), NOT Peloton Interactive. Merck deal was ~$1.05B upfront plus up to $1.15B milestones. An academic scientist; best route is UTSW media relations. Wikipedia notes a 2014 ASBMB column controversy - avoid.

current_role: Co-founder of ShopClues (former Chief Business Officer); current role not verified
profile: Radhika Aggarwal co-founded ShopClues, an Indian online marketplace for value-focused shoppers in smaller cities, in July 2011 with Sanjay Sethi and Sandeep Aggarwal, serving as Chief Business Officer.
